mission:
Fix a bug: `overlaps` in src/overlaps.js returns true for intervals that only touch at one end when either interval is marked half-open.
Support an optional `open: true` property on an interval, meaning its end point is excluded: `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` must be false, while the same call without `open` stays true.
Keep the existing behaviour for intervals without `open`, add regression tests next to the existing ones, and keep `npm test` passing.

plan.summary: Fix `overlaps` in src/overlaps.js (currently `a.start <= b.end && b.start <= a.end` at line 3, which ignores any `open` flag) so that an interval with `open: true` excludes its end point. Each of the two comparisons becomes strict when the interval whose `end` is being compared is open. Intervals without `open` keep the closed behaviour. Regression tests go in test/overlaps.test.js beside the two existing tests. This is one small task, since the fix and its tests are a single coherent change across two files. I could not run `npm test` as planner (the read-only hook blocks npm), so the baseline suite state is unverified.
assumptions: `open: true` excludes only the interval's `end` point; `start` is always included (half-open [start, end)), as the request states.
Only a truthy `open` changes behaviour; `open` missing, `false` or `undefined` means a closed interval.
The flag applies symmetrically: `overlaps({start:3,end:5}, {start:1,end:3,open:true})` is also false, as the request says 'either interval'.
A degenerate empty open interval (start === end with `open: true`) is out of scope and gets no special handling.
No input validation, TypeScript types or README changes are required; the README does not document the API.
The existing tests pass at HEAD 3f754a2. This was not verified, because the planner role is not permitted to run npm.
acceptanceCriteria: `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns false.
`overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3 }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` still returns true.
With the arguments swapped, `overlaps({ start: 3, end: 5 }, { start: 1, end: 3, open: true })` returns false.
The two existing tests in test/overlaps.test.js are unchanged and still pass.
New regression tests for `open` exist in test/overlaps.test.js, and `npm test` exits 0.

tasks.title: Honour `open: true` in overlaps and add regression tests
tasks.description:
Repository: plain ESM JavaScript package (package.json has "type": "module" and test script `node --test`, no dependencies). src/overlaps.js exports `overlaps(a, b)`, currently implemented as `return a.start <= b.end && b.start <= a.end` with a JSDoc line describing closed intervals. It ignores an optional `open` property, so intervals that only touch at one end are reported as overlapping even when one is half-open.

Change `overlaps` so an interval with a truthy `open` property excludes its `end` point (half-open [start, end)); `start` is always included. Concretely, the comparison against `b.end` must be strict (`a.start < b.end`) when `b.open` is truthy, and the comparison against `a.end` must be strict (`b.start < a.end`) when `a.open` is truthy; otherwise keep `<=`. Intervals without `open` must behave exactly as before. Update the one-line JSDoc comment to mention the optional `open` flag. Keep the implementation minimal: no validation, no new files, no new exports, and do not touch src/index.js.

Add regression tests to test/overlaps.test.js beside the two existing tests, in the same style (node:test, `node:assert/strict`, one-line `test(...)` calls importing from '../src/index.js'). Do not modify or remove the existing tests. Cover: (1) `{start:1,end:3,open:true}` vs `{start:3,end:5}` is false; (2) the same with arguments swapped is false; (3) open on the interval whose end is not the touching point, `{start:1,end:3}` vs `{start:3,end:5,open:true}`, is still true; (4) both open and touching, `{start:1,end:3,open:true}` vs `{start:3,end:5,open:true}`, is false; (5) open intervals that genuinely overlap, e.g. `{start:1,end:4,open:true}` vs `{start:3,end:5}`, are true; (6) `open: false` on touching intervals is true.

Run `npm test` from the repository root and confirm it exits 0 with all tests passing. The environment is native Windows with PowerShell.
acceptanceCriteria: `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns false, and returns false with the arguments swapped.
`overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3 }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns true, and `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 2 }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns false.
`overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3 }, { start: 3, end: 5, open: true })` returns true, because the open end 5 is not the touching point.
`overlaps({ start: 1, end: 4, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns true.
test/overlaps.test.js keeps the two original tests unmodified and adds tests for the cases above.
`npm test` exits 0 with no failing or skipped tests.
`git diff --stat` shows changes only in src/overlaps.js and test/overlaps.test.js.

risks.description: The strictness could be attached to the wrong comparison, for example making `a.start < b.end` strict when `a.open` is set. The headline example would then still be wrong, or the fix would work in one argument order only.
risks.mitigation: The task spells out which comparison pairs with which interval's flag and requires tests in both argument orders, plus a case where the open end is not the touching point.

risks.description: Closed-interval behaviour could regress for existing callers.
risks.mitigation: The existing tests must stay unmodified and passing, and a test for explicit `open: false` is added.

risks.description: Baseline `npm test` status was not verified during planning, because the planner hook blocks npm.
risks.mitigation: The worker runs `npm test` and reports the actual output. Any pre-existing failure should be reported, not hidden by changing tests.

reviews.summary: No concrete defects found. The implementation matches the open-end comparison requirements, keeps src/index.js untouched, preserves the two original tests, and adds the requested regression cases. I could not independently rerun npm test because local command policy blocked npm/node execution, but the supplied test output reports all 8 tests passing.
